heading: Questions about working with me
intro: Straight answers to the questions I'm asked most, about fees, timing and how business and property lending fit together.
seo_title: Mortgage adviser FAQs | GB Mortgages, Queenstown
seo_description: Answers to common questions about using a mortgage adviser in Queenstown: what I do, how I'm paid, fees, and business and property lending.

items.q: What does a mortgage adviser do?
a: A mortgage adviser finds the lending that fits your situation and manages the application for you. I look at your income, assets and plans, choose the lenders that suit, and prepare your application in the terms each lender uses to assess it. I deal with the lenders for you and stay in touch through settlement and after it.

items.q: Why use a mortgage broker instead of going straight to my bank?
a: Your bank can only offer its own loans. I compare several lenders, and I know how each one assesses business income, rental income and construction lending. That affects how much you can borrow, how your loan is structured and which lender is likely to approve it.

items.q: Do you charge fees for mortgage advice?
a: For most home and investment property loans, I don't charge a fee. The lender pays me a commission when your loan settles.
I may charge a one-off fee in two situations:

ol: The lender doesn't pay commission. This can happen with some business, commercial and non-bank lenders, or if you ask me to arrange a product outside my usual lender arrangements. The fee is based on the time I expect to spend, and we agree it in writing before I start. For business and commercial lending, it goes in a letter of engagement. If the lender also pays me commission, I take that amount off your fee.

I have to repay commission to the lender. This applies if, within 28 months of drawdown, your loan is fully or partly repaid or its terms change materially, and the lender asks for its commission back. The fee is $250 an hour for the time I spent on your loan, up to $2,500, and never more than the commission I repay.

a: You pay other costs, such as lender fees, valuations and legal fees, to those parties. I'll tell you about any I know of before you go ahead. My disclosure statement has the full detail.

items.q: Will I pay a fee if I refinance within 28 months?
a: Only if the lender asks me to repay my commission. That can happen if, within 28 months of drawdown, your loan is fully or partly repaid or its terms change materially. The fee is $250 an hour for the time I spent on your loan, up to $2,500, and never more than the commission I repay. Talk to me before you refinance or repay early, and I'll tell you whether a fee applies.

items.q: Do you only do home loans?
a: No. I arrange home loans, investment property lending, business lending, and lending for commercial builds and developments. Many of my clients have more than one of these, so I manage them together.
items.plain: No. I arrange home loans, investment property lending, business lending, and lending for commercial builds and developments. Many of my clients have more than one of these, so I manage them together.

items.q: Can you manage my business and personal lending together?
a: Yes. I spent most of my banking career working with business owners who also held residential property. I look at the whole position, so your business lending and property lending are structured to work together. You tell your story once.

items.q: Can I use my business to buy an investment property?
a: Often, yes. Some lenders will count your business's balance sheet and spare cash flow towards buying residential or commercial property. Each lender treats business income differently, and the structure matters: who owns the property, what is used as security and whether you give a personal guarantee. Before you commit, I'll show you what each lender will look at.

items.q: How much of my time will the mortgage process take?
a: About an hour to start, then a few minutes to upload your documents. We meet in person or online, during the day or in the evening. After that, I send you a link to my secure client portal. It lists the documents I need based on your answers, and you upload them when it suits you. I deal with the lenders from there.

items.q: Do I need to understand my finances before I see a mortgage adviser?
a: No, that's my job. Many clients come to me unsure how their finances fit together. We go through it at your pace, in plain language. By the end, you'll know where you stand and what your options are.
